name: Focus and selection continuity
when: Use only when an evidenced focus interaction needs feedback or continuity; optional motion is not a product requirement.
problem: Keyboard users need an immediate, unambiguous indication of the current actionable control without competing visual contours.
animate: Prefer one intentional integrated focus treatment on already bordered controls when contrast suffices; a clear border change can replace an added ring. External outlines remain valid for accessibility, contrasting surfaces or design-system consistency.
stable: Keep border width, control dimensions, content position and reading order stable across focus and blur; show the indicator immediately without layout shifts or unnecessary transitions.
easing: Prefer ease-out for arrivals; ease-in for departures; keep direct manipulation immediate.
accessibility: Keyboard focus must remain clearly visible. Replace browser defaults only with a suitable accessible alternative; evaluate contrast and recognition on light/dark surfaces and normal, invalid, disabled and read-only states.
reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, remove spatial movement and looping effects; retain an instant state change and textual feedback.
performance: Prefer opacity/transform on small elements; avoid per-frame layout, large blur/repaint regions and permanent will-change hints.
avoid: Avoid accidental border/outline/shadow stacking: a double contour is not automatically better. Never remove keyboard visibility or globally suppress outlines; distinguish focused and invalid states with explicit error feedback.
